current_profile.name: Cardiac Arrhythmia (e.g. Atrial Fibrillation, SVT)
current_profile.round_u_followup_provenance: typical_features 'syncope without warning' and 'palpitations before syncope' added in the Round U follow-up: syncope without prodrome (or with a very short one) and sudden palpitation immediately followed by syncope are listed among the high-risk features suggesting arrhythmic syncope (Brignole M et al., 2018 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope, Eur Heart J 2018;39:1883-1948, Table 5, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehy037). It supports the arrhythmia CATEGORY only; it never identifies a rhythm subtype, and danger adds no score. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.
current_profile.round_q_provenance: typical_features 'pulse rate below 50' / 'pulse rate of 150 or more' added in Round Q: a measured CURRENT rate at the thresholds the AHA adult bradycardia/tachycardia algorithms use to suggest a rhythm cause (Panchal AR et al., 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC Part 3, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468). Weighted like a generic physiological sign (the reduced multiplier differential.py gives tachycardia/hypotension); not a confirmatory finding and never a subtype. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.

current_profile.name: Severe Electrolyte Disorder (e.g. Hyperkalemia/Hyponatremia)
current_profile.round_q_provenance: Round Q: risk factor 'missed dialysis session' -- missed or inadequate dialysis is a recognised cause of hyperkalaemia in people on dialysis (UK Kidney Association, Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Acute Hyperkalaemia in Adults, 2020/2023 update, causes section). Risk-factor weight only; it never establishes a potassium value or direction. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.
current_profile.round_p_provenance: Round P: hypokalemia / low potassium / prominent U waves added as confirmatory findings and muscle cramps as a typical feature -- the entry already covered both directions of sodium but only the high direction of potassium, so a severely LOW potassium was scored as evidence AGAINST the disorder. Agent-authored from widely taught physiology; not clinician-reviewed.

evidence_references.scope: History, examination and urine investigations inform diagnosis; this internal abstention guard is not a guideline diagnostic criterion.

current_profile.name: Sepsis
current_profile.post_round_w_provenance: typical_features 'mottled skin on examination', 'temperature below 36 degrees' and 'grunting on examination' added post-Round-W: they are NICE NG51 (Sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management, 2016, updated 2024) high-risk criteria observable without any test -- mottled or ashen appearance (all ages), temperature below 36 C (all ages), grunting (children under 5). The temperature feature is SUPPORT-ONLY and decided by the measured value (a fever does not contradict it: hypothermia is an alternative presentation, not a defining sign); the two signs are examination findings, never asked as questions. They support the working diagnosis of suspected sepsis; they do not identify a source or organism and danger adds no score. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.

current_profile.name: Ischemic Stroke
current_profile.round_u_followup_provenance: typical_feature 'focal neurological deficit on examination' added in the Round U follow-up: stroke is an episode of acute neurological dysfunction caused by focal cerebral infarction (Sacco RL et al., An Updated Definition of Stroke, Stroke 2013;44:2064-2089), presenting with a sudden focal neurological deficit (Powers WJ et al., 2019 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline, Stroke 2019;50:e344). It is an examination finding (objective-only); it is not imaging confirmation and danger adds no score. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.

current_profile.name: Bacterial Meningitis

evidence_references.scope: Clinical features and investigation results are combined; this software final-label guard does not exclude meningitis or suppress urgent evaluation.

current_profile.post_round_w_provenance: typical_features 'bulging fontanelle on examination' and 'high-pitched cry on examination' added post-Round-W: NICE NG143 (Fever in under 5s, Table 1 'traffic light' red features: bulging fontanelle; weak, high-pitched or continuous cry) and NICE NG240 (Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease, 2024: symptoms and signs in infants include a bulging fontanelle and irritability/abnormal cry). They are signs observed by the examiner or reported by a caregiver, never asked as questions, and only occur in infants with an open fontanelle. They support the working diagnosis of suspected bacterial meningitis; they do not confirm it (no CSF), and danger adds no score. Agent-authored, not clinician-reviewed.

priority_review_questions.title: 진정수면제 의존과 사용장애의 구분
priority_review_questions.observation: 용량 증가·금단·감량 어려움만으로 사용장애를 선택할 수 있음. 치료 중 생리적 의존과 사용장애의 동등성은 입증되지 않음.
priority_review_questions.review_question: 처방대로 복용하던 환자의 금단을 사용장애로 단정하지 않는지, 기능 손상·조절 실패·유해 사용 조건과 명칭을 검토.
